A small, dependency-free RSS reader.
Paste a link, get a clean place to read.

What it is
Reader is a local web app that turns RSS, Atom and JSON feeds into a three-pane
reading experience: your feeds on the left, headlines in the middle, the article
on the right. It runs on Node.js with
no npm dependencies and no build step
—

No accounts, no cloud, no analytics. Everything stays in a JSON file on your machine.
No CORS problems: the server fetches feeds, not your browser.
No full-text extraction or scraping: it shows what the feed publishes, plus a link
to the original.

What to do

Security and limitations
Local app, no authentication.
Don't expose it to the internet as-is. If you
need remote access, put it behind a reverse proxy with auth (and HTTPS).
The server will fetch whatever URL you give it, including internal addresses.
Only run it for people you trust.
Article content is sanitized and sandboxed, but it is still third-party HTML.
External images load from their original sites.
Single user, no sync, no full-text extraction, no offline images, no push.
No automated tests — verify changes against a couple of real feeds.

and readable so a human can audit or extend it. If you find rough edges, that's why.
If you build on it: the server is framework-free
node:http
, the frontend is
vanilla DOM, and both are small enough to read in an afternoon.

Apache License 2.0 — see
LICENSE

Will it slow down my PC or drain the battery?
Most themes use lightweight 2D rendering and won’t noticeably affect performance or battery life. They animate only when the desktop is visible and pause whenever a full-screen app or maximized window is in front.
Does it read my files?

You heal and get mana back only while fed. You do not eat by hand: whenever your stomach is empty, the bag eats a food for you. With nothing to eat you lose a hitpoint every 10 seconds, down to your last, except in a protection zone
Potions
Click one in your bag to drink it. A health potion heals and a mana potion restores mana, over a few seconds rather than at once
Experience and levels
Killing monsters earns experience, which floats up over your head. Everybody who hurt a monster gets its whole experience. Each level gives you more hitpoints, mana, speed and carrying capacity, and makes health and mana come back faster. The stats panel shows your XP rate an hour and how long the next level will take
Skills
Fist, melee, ranged, shielding, magic and fishing. Each is trained by using it: every swing, shot, blocked blow or catch. Magic is trained by spending mana. Higher skill makes your gear hit, block or catch better. See the Skills panel’s own help
Spells
A spell is cast by saying its words into the chat box, or by pressing its icon in the Spells panel, which lists every spell your mana can pay for, cheapest first. Hover or hold an icon for what it does. Green will go off, gold will go off but waste the mana, red will be refused, with the reason. Spells have cooldowns. Everyone near you hears the words. A spell that calls up a creature opens a list of the ones you can call; press the
☆
beside one to pin it to the top of that list, and the
★
to unpin it
Fighting
Your attack, defense and armor are on the stats panel. Every blow is rolled: it can do anything from a little to its most. Your
defense
— your shield’s block and your weapon’s parry — meets each blow first, but only the first two blows every two seconds, so a crowd gets past it. Your
armor
meets every blow after that.
Shots go past your defense
and meet your armor alone, and do not count among those two blows. A shield is armor as well as a block: its block, before skill, counts in your armor too.
Changing what is in your hands takes a moment
: a weapon just taken up swings no sooner than a second later, and a shield just raised blocks nothing for a second. The log says what hit you and with what
Ranged weapons
A bow or crossbow shoots your target from a distance, along a clear line: over water, but not through walls. Every shot uses an arrow or bolt from your bag, and with none you do not shoot. Shots miss more often while you are moving; stand still to shoot true. A shot goes past a monster’s defense and meets its armor alone, as shots at you meet only yours
Cleave and reach
A weapon marked
cleave
carries a killing blow on: whatever the blow had left over after the kill goes into the nearest monster within the weapon’s reach, where its armor and defense meet it as they would any blow, and if that kills it too the rest goes on again. It never goes into a person. A long weapon marked
reach
strikes that many tiles away along a clear line, thrust rather than shot
Poison and other harm
Some attacks poison, burn, slow or hold you. Poison bites every two seconds, a little less each time, and armor is no answer to it. The badge in the top left shows it, and your health bar turns green for what the poison will still take. Dying clears it
Noise and sight
Monsters notice you by what they hear and see. Your
clank
, on the stats panel, is how much noise you make; the less, the closer you can get before something notices you. A creature can only see you within its sight, and at night or underground that is short unless you carry a light
Running away
A monster follows you only so far before it gives up and wanders home, but while you keep hitting it, it keeps after you. Some monsters run when badly hurt
The dark
Under the ground, and above it at night, you see only what is lit and the tile or so round you. A torch held in your off hand lights the ground round you, and so does a light spell. A torch burns only while held in the dark, and the next one in your bag is lit when it gutters out. A light can be seen from as far as it reaches
Day and night
Above the ground, seven minutes of day, then three of night, the same for everybody
Protection zones
Safe ground, such as the starting village, towns and the ground round the world’s people. Nothing can be fought there, monsters cannot come in, and you never starve, but mana does not come back. The shield badge shows while you stand in one
Where you start
New characters wake in Hobbiton’s protection zone with a little gear, food and a potion, and that is where you come back after dying
Logging back in
You come back where you logged out, or on the nearest free tile
Death
Dying costs a tenth of your experience and of the practice under every skill, and every coin you carry spills where you fell. Now and then something else in your bag drops too. Your gear and everything else come back with you to the temple. Store what you value in the depot
Fighting players
Your stance says whom you may attack. Whoever you attack may fight back. Nobody may attack a player under half their level unless that player wears a skull. Attacking a player who is not protection zone locked and has not attacked you locks you: your eyes go red, and you cannot log out until the fight is over. Killing such a player puts a skull on you for a time, and a skull keeps you out of protection zones
Bosses
A boss is a monster played by an admin: its name is in the monsters’ colour and a look says it is a boss. Fight it as you would a monster
Gear
The best weapon, shield, armor, helm, cloak and belt in your bag are used for you, and outlined. Click a piece to use that one instead; click it again to go back to the best. Rings are worn only when you click them. Hover any item for what it does. The colour of the outline round an item says who made it, and its tooltip says what that adds
Wear and tear
Gear can break in use. When it does it is gone, and the next best thing in your bag takes over
Weight
Everything weighs something, counted in coins (cn), the weight of one gold coin. What you can carry grows with your level, and a belt adds more. The bag’s icon fills as you load it. Past the line it turns red and fills again from the bottom: you can carry up to twice as much, but you walk at half pace, though a horse is not slowed. When the red is full you can pick nothing more up
Your bag
Holds any number of kinds of thing, limited only by weight. Everything stacks
Loot
A monster sometimes leaves loot beside its body when it dies: gold and other things, picked up off the ground like anything else. A body lasts a few minutes, then rots away
Shops
Some of the world’s people keep shops: click them and choose Trade. They sell their wares and buy most things for a fifth of what they are worth. While a shop is open your bag shows what it pays for each pile
Depot
Storage boxes stand in several towns, and every box opens the same depot. Stand beside one and press the chest icon. It holds anything, as much as you like, and what is in it is safe when you die
Market
The market is open at every depot box, for trading with other players: list things from your depot at a price, or buy what others have listed. Unsold prices fall over time. Gold from sales waits to be collected
Quests
Many of the world’s people want something: ask them about what they talk about. A quest pays once per life, and dying lets you do it again. When somebody sends you somewhere, it is marked on your map
Your map
The map fills in as you explore and is kept with your character. Zoom out for the map of where you have been. Click into the black to walk there if there is a way
Floors
Stairs, ramps, ladders and holes take you up and down. Buildings show their roofs from outside, and lift them while you are inside. Use the floor chip to look up or down
Somebody in your way
Walk into another player standing still and they step aside. A monster smaller than you is pushed aside too; one your own size or bigger stands its ground. Walking into things pushes them and never crushes them
Fishing
Take a fishing rod in hand and it casts by itself at any fish you can see within a few tiles. Every catch trains fishing
Dropped skulls
A death leaves a skull where it happened, its eyes in the colour of whoever died
Announcements
Everyone online is told when a player enters or leaves the world, is slain, or advances a level
Choose your race
Every character is one of the free peoples of Middle-earth, and each is good at something and pays for it somewhere else. Your choice is kept; while races are not locked in, /race brings this window back at your next login. The help’s Race entry has the numbers.
Elf
The Firstborn. More mana, quicker at magic and the bow, and snow is no hindrance; less health.
Man
The Followers. Ordinary health and mana, and a tenth quicker to learn every skill.
Dwarf
Durin’s folk. The most health, quicker at melee and shielding; little mana.
Hobbit
Halflings of the Shire. Hardly heard, a meal goes half as far again, quicker with the bow and the rod; less health.

The world, still being played. The box has no wash under it, it takes no keys, and the arrows still walk you while it is open — so a potion can be drunk out of it while you are backing away from something

It opens by itself when a trade window or a shop does, since you trade out of it, stays shown for as long as the window is up, and closes again at the end unless you had it open already

The same as a right-click: the same menu, on a touchscreen

TLS connection with the Relay server until client ticket check

in parallel with the live Relay server connection, clients also try to create a direct connection between each other, and switch to it if successful (this can be turned off)
IPC encryption:
communication between processes is also encrypted with TLS 1.3
Transparency:
data communication can be checked by turning on debug logging
Saved remote passwords:
double encryption, encrypted by both the remote machine and the client side with their own keys, cannot be decrypted on either side without the other

Questions
Is PicoDiet free?
Yes. There is no sign-up and no watermark. Each batch takes up to 30 images, each up to 25 megapixels and 30 MB.
Will my images lose quality?
Not visibly at the default setting. Lossy compression removes information, but PicoDiet keeps only results that score at least 80 on SSIMULACRA2, which looks the same as the original at normal viewing distance. Set 90 or more if the images will be inspected up close or edited again.
How much smaller do files get?
It depends on the image. In our tests at the default setting, a camera JPEG shrank 87%, a Retina screenshot saved as PNG 77%, a photo exported as WebP 33%, and a 12-megapixel iPhone photo became, with Auto, a JPEG 83% smaller than its HEIC at 1920 pixels. Which formats can I upload?
PNG, JPEG (also .jfif), WebP, GIF (animated too), AVIF, HEIC/HEIF from iPhones, BMP and TIFF. BMP and TIFF come back as PNG, or as JPEG for photos. Results can be JPEG, PNG, WebP or AVIF, and animations can be GIF, WebP or animated PNG.
Does it remove photo metadata?
Yes, from every file PicoDiet makes: camera data and location (EXIF, GPS) are removed, and the colour profile is kept so colours look the same. When your original is already the smallest, PicoDiet gives it back unchanged, metadata included.
Are my images private?
